verdict.rationale: pnpm's own docs say dependency install scripts are blocked by default and that you approve which packages may run build scripts, which covers the lifecycle-script half of the story directly. Registry signature verification via audit adds another anti-tampering control. Minimum release age is not in first-party docs: it appears only in community threads that ask where the minimumReleaseAge setting lives and whether it works globally, so that half rests on indirect evidence. missing for 10: first-party documentation of minimumReleaseAge (configuration, scope, enforcement), detailed docs on the build-script allowlist settings, independent hands-on corroboration that both protections work.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can turn on protections against malicious packages, such as blocking lifecycle scripts or enforcing a minimum release age

citations.quote: Install scripts don't run for arbitrary dependencies. You approve which packages may execute build scripts — supply-chain safety without extra tooling.
Verifies the ECDSA registry signatures of installed packages against the public keys published by each registry at `/-/npm/v1/keys`.
